target_customer: Small and mid-size US importers and wholesalers (foodservice supply, builders, pet supply, industrial parts) buying pallets to containers from Chinese factories
problem: Small importers buy through several middlemen who each add margin, and quotes float with freight, FX and tariffs, so they cannot lock a landed price.
business_model: Trading company: buys from factories and resells at one locked delivered price, margin on goods

founders.name: Benjamin Martindale
education: University of Toronto Rotman, finance, one credit short of finishing
founders.background_notes: YC page says he grew up in his family's importing business in Toronto, advised Chinese heavy-machinery companies selling to the West, and ran a Wuhan office.

founders.name: Minghao Tan
founders.background_notes: Builds the data side, parsing customs filings. The YC launch post mentions a co-founder named James from InstaLILY; whether this is Tan is unconfirmed.

competitors.name: AiDeliv
competitors.what: AI DDP marketplace pooling small shippers so carriers bid to lock total landed cost

competitors.name: Alibaba Accio Work
competitors.what: AI agent for SMEs that runs supplier RFQs, negotiation and customs paperwork

competitors.name: Flexport
competitors.what: Freight forwarder and customs platform with landed cost reporting

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching customs records to real factories and computing duty and container packing is moderate data engineering; the hard parts are operational (inspection, credit, tariff risk).

defensibility.rationale: Factory relationships and shared container volume could compound, but the pitch is copyable and the company carries tariff and FX risk on locked prices.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Alibaba launched AI sourcing agents in 2026 aimed at the same SME buyers; no action against Donkey reported.

market_need_then: Small importers face stacked middleman markups and volatile tariffs in 2025 and 2026, so a locked all-in price is a clear pain point. Demand evidence is the founder's claim, not independent data.

branding.domain_note: Uses donkey.trade, not the exact .com; no purchase story found

identity.logo: Logo present, not described in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident short declaratives, e.g. 'If freight or tariffs move after that, that's our problem.'

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable plain word and a clear tagline, but no press about the brand and the name has no stated tie to trading.

outcome_analysis: Donkey is a Summer 2026 YC company with five people and no reported exit or distress. It sells a risky, working-capital heavy trading model to small importers while Alibaba and AiDeliv launched AI sourcing tools in 2026. Too early to judge success or failure.
notes: Unverified: Dealroom lists a $125k seed round with no investor or date; single aggregator, not recorded as a round. RuntimeWire says no Donkey-specific financing is disclosed. Team size 5 on YC, 7 on another page. Site mentions Shenzhen, YC page mentions Wuhan. An aggregator claims Martindale built Prelude OS; not verified so not recorded. Completeness pass: the 125K seed rests on a single database (Dealroom) with no date or investors; no press confirms it.
